topic: Thomson, Rutherford and Bohr Atomic Models
title: Atom Models: Melon to Orbits Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
A watermelon full of seeds, a cricket ball in a huge stadium, and a staircase you climb step by step. Each one was once our best picture of the atom. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 2, Structure of Atom) we follow how the model of the atom changed, twice.

Thomson's model (1898) spreads positive charge through a sphere with electrons inside, like seeds in a watermelon. On the molecule bench, alpha particles fly at a gold foil about 100 nm thick, each on a path bent by the repulsion of a nucleus: most pass straight, a few bend, and about 1 in 20,000 bounce almost straight back. Link by link we reach Rutherford's nucleus (about 10^-15 m in an atom of about 10^-10 m) and his planet-like model, then see why it fails: a circling electron accelerates, radiates energy and would spiral in within about 10^-8 s. Bohr's rules (1913) fix it: fixed orbits, En = -2.18 × 10^-18 (1/n^2) J, a photon for every jump, and rn = 52.9 n^2 pm. A worked example finds the energy for the jump from n = 1 to n = 2 and the radius of orbit 2, then the exam trap about the minus sign, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 15 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students.
